@@ -0,0 +1,84 @@
+# docker/ - container builds per shipped target
+
+The release artifacts are built by `.github/workflows/release.yml` on a
+`vX.Y.0` tag. This directory lets anyone with Docker (BuildKit) rebuild the
+Linux packages locally from the same scripts, and cross-build Windows
+binaries for testing, without a GitHub runner and without spending Actions
+minutes. No workflow runs these images: they are local tooling.
+
+Run every command from the repository root (the build context is the repo;
+`.dockerignore` keeps `target/`, `dist/`, `.git` and `.claude/` out of it).
+
+| Shipped target | In Docker? | How |
+|---|---|---|
+| Linux x86_64 tar.gz, deb, rpm, AppImage | yes | `docker/linux.Dockerfile` |
+| Linux snap | no - stays on the runner | see "Snap and Flatpak" |
+| Linux Flatpak | no - stays on the runner | see "Snap and Flatpak" |
+| Windows zip + Inno installer (msvc) | no - stays on the runner | see "Windows" |
+| Windows portable zip (gnu, unofficial) | yes, cross from Linux | `docker/windows-gnu.Dockerfile` |
+| macOS universal zip + dmg | no - stays on the runner | see "macOS" |
+
+## Linux
+
+    docker build -f docker/linux.Dockerfile --output type=local,dest=dist .
+    # or: docker/build.sh
+
+`dist/` receives `camcraft-<ver>-linux-x86_64.{tar.gz,deb,rpm,AppImage}`.
+The image mirrors the release `linux` job: the `ubuntu-22.04` base (pinned
+by digest), its apt package list verbatim, the same `cargo build --locked
+--release` line, `scripts/package-linux.sh`, `scripts/package-appimage.sh`
+with the same pinned linuxdeploy and SHA-256, and the job's package-content
+checks. Differences from the hosted runner, all forced by a bare image:
+
+- `build-essential`, `ca-certificates`, `curl` and `file` are installed
+  (the runner has them preinstalled; flecs' C sources need the compiler).
+- Rust is pinned (`--build-arg RUST_TOOLCHAIN=...`, default 1.99.1) where
+  the runner uses whatever stable it ships that week. Keep it at or above
+  the workspace `rust-version`.
+- The AppImage is assembled without FUSE: `package-appimage.sh` only
+  extracts linuxdeploy and runs its bundled appimagetool, which works in an
+  unprivileged container.
+
+BuildKit cache mounts keep the cargo registry and `target/` between runs, so
+a rebuild after a source edit recompiles only what changed.
+
+## Snap and Flatpak
+
+Both stay on the `snap` / `flatpak` runner jobs. `snapcraft` needs a running
+`snapd` (systemd, snap confinement), and `flatpak-builder` builds inside
+`bwrap` sandboxes that need user namespaces and mounts; both need a
+`--privileged` container at best, which a reproducible build image should
+not ask for. Both only repackage the Linux tarball, so a tarball from the
+Linux image can be fed to `scripts/package-snap.sh` /
+`scripts/package-flatpak.sh` on a Linux host that has those tools.
+
+## Windows
+
+The shipped Windows build stays native on `windows-latest`:
+
+- It is an **msvc** build (`x86_64-pc-windows-msvc`), and the installer is
+  built by Inno Setup (`scripts/installer.ps1`, ISCC.exe) and optionally
+  signed by `signtool` (`scripts/sign.ps1`) - all Windows-only tools.
+  Cross-building msvc from Linux (cargo-xwin) would mean downloading the
+  Microsoft CRT and Windows SDK under their license, inside an image we
+  would then distribute; we do not do that.
+
+`docker/windows-gnu.Dockerfile` instead cross-compiles the
+**x86_64-pc-windows-gnu** target with mingw-w64 (the C cross compiler builds
+flecs' sources; wgpu, winit and rfd are pure Rust on Windows) and packs a
+portable zip with the release zip's layout, named `...-win-x64-gnu.zip` so
+it is never mistaken for a release asset:
+
+    docker build -f docker/windows-gnu.Dockerfile --output type=local,dest=dist .
+    # or: docker/build.sh windows
+
+It is for building and hand-testing Windows binaries from a Linux or macOS
+machine. It is unsigned, has no installer, and links the mingw runtime
+instead of the MSVC one, so it is not published.
+
+## macOS
+
+Stays on the `macos-15` runner. Building for Apple targets needs the macOS
+SDK and Apple's linker, and Apple's Xcode/SDK license allows them only on
+Apple hardware; `hdiutil` (the dmg) exists only on macOS. A Linux container
+cannot build the universal app legally, so there is no macOS image.

+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# Build CamCraft's containerised targets and copy the packages to dist/.
+# Provenance: docker/README.md; `docker build --output` (BuildKit) docs.
+#   docker/build.sh            # linux (tar.gz, deb, rpm, AppImage)
+#   docker/build.sh windows    # windows-gnu portable zip (unofficial)
+#   docker/build.sh all
+set -euo pipefail
+root=$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)
+cd "$root"
+command -v docker >/dev/null || { echo "docker/build.sh: docker is not on PATH" >&2; exit 1; }
+targets=("${@:-linux}")
+[[ ${targets[0]} == all ]] && targets=(linux windows)
+for t in "${targets[@]}"; do
+    case $t in
+        linux) file=docker/linux.Dockerfile ;;
+        windows) file=docker/windows-gnu.Dockerfile ;;
+        *) echo "docker/build.sh: unknown target '$t' (linux, windows, all)" >&2; exit 2 ;;
+    esac
+    DOCKER_BUILDKIT=1 docker build -f "$file" --target packages \
+        --output "type=local,dest=dist" .
+done
+ls -l dist

+# syntax=docker/dockerfile:1
+# Linux x86_64 release build in a container: the same tar.gz, deb, rpm and
+# AppImage the release.yml `linux` job ships, from the same scripts.
+# Provenance: CamCraft's .github/workflows/release.yml (linux job) and the
+# Dockerfile reference (docs.docker.com/reference/dockerfile).
+#
+#   docker build -f docker/linux.Dockerfile --output type=local,dest=dist .
+#
+# Pinned to the runner's distro (ubuntu-22.04: glibc 2.35, which the .deb's
+# `libc6 (>= 2.35)` dependency names) by digest, so a rebuild sees the
+# same base the day it was pinned.
+FROM ubuntu:22.04@sha256:076e7bf82319619f28dd0aa9c02ab34b055ad37100395b4f49a2ffba04fb5e11 AS toolchain
+
+ARG DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive
+# release.yml's "Install Linux build and package tools" list, verbatim,
+# plus what the hosted runner has preinstalled and a bare image lacks:
+# a C toolchain (flecs_ecs_sys compiles flecs.c through the cc crate),
+# curl + ca-certificates (rustup, linuxdeploy) and file (linuxdeploy).
+RUN apt-get update \
+ && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
+        pkg-config libwayland-dev libxkbcommon-dev libx11-dev rpm imagemagick \
+        build-essential ca-certificates curl file \
+ && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*
+
+# The hosted runner builds with its preinstalled stable Rust; the container
+# pins one so two builds of one commit use one compiler. Must stay >= the
+# workspace rust-version (Cargo.toml, 1.90). Override with
+# --build-arg RUST_TOOLCHAIN=<version>.
+ARG RUST_TOOLCHAIN=1.99.1
+ENV RUSTUP_HOME=/usr/local/rustup \
+    CARGO_HOME=/usr/local/cargo \
+    PATH=/usr/local/cargo/bin:$PATH
+RUN curl --proto '=https' --tlsv1.2 -LfsS https://sh.rustup.rs \
+        | sh -s -- -y --no-modify-path --profile minimal \
+            --default-toolchain "$RUST_TOOLCHAIN" \
+ && rustc --version && cargo --version
+
+# release.yml's "Install pinned linuxdeploy" step: same URL, same SHA-256.
+# package-appimage.sh only --appimage-extract's it and runs the bundled
+# appimagetool, so no FUSE is needed inside the container.
+RUN curl -LfsS -o /opt/linuxdeploy-x86_64.AppImage \
+        https://github.com/linuxdeploy/linuxdeploy/releases/download/1-alpha-20251107-1/linuxdeploy-x86_64.AppImage \
+ && echo 'c20cd71e3a4e3b80c3483cef793cda3f4e990aca14014d23c544ca3ce1270b4d  /opt/linuxdeploy-x86_64.AppImage' | sha256sum -c - \
+ && chmod +x /opt/linuxdeploy-x86_64.AppImage
+
+FROM toolchain AS build
+WORKDIR /src
+COPY . .
+# release.yml's "Build release binaries" step, verbatim. The cache mounts
+# keep the registry and target/ between `docker build` runs (BuildKit).
+RUN --mount=type=cache,target=/usr/local/cargo/registry \
+    --mount=type=cache,target=/src/target \
+    cargo build --locked --release -p camcraft-ui -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-post \
+ && mkdir -p /out/bin \
+ && cp target/release/camcraft-ui target/release/camcraft-cli target/release/post /out/bin/
+# "Assemble Linux packages" and "Assemble AppImage", from the copied-out
+# binaries (the target/ cache mount is gone after the RUN above).
+ENV CAMCRAFT_BIN_DIR=/out/bin \
+    CAMCRAFT_DIST_DIR=/src/dist \
+    LINUXDEPLOY=/opt/linuxdeploy-x86_64.AppImage
+RUN scripts/package-linux.sh && scripts/package-appimage.sh
+# release.yml's "Check package contents", minus the runner paths.
+RUN tar -tzf dist/*.tar.gz | grep '/camcraft-ui$' \
+ && dpkg-deb --contents dist/*.deb | grep '/usr/lib/camcraft/camcraft-ui$' \
+ && rpm -qpl dist/*.rpm | grep '/usr/lib/camcraft/camcraft-ui$' \
+ && test -s dist/*.AppImage \
+ && check=$(mktemp -d) \
+ && (cd "$check" && /src/dist/*.AppImage --appimage-extract >/dev/null) \
+ && cmp /out/bin/camcraft-ui "$check/squashfs-root/usr/bin/camcraft-ui" \
+ && test -x "$check/squashfs-root/AppRun" \
+ && test -d "$check/squashfs-root/usr/bin/assets/themes" \
+ && rm -rf "$check"
+
+# `--output type=local,dest=dist` writes exactly these files to the host.
+FROM scratch AS packages
+COPY --from=build /src/dist/*.tar.gz /src/dist/*.deb /src/dist/*.rpm /src/dist/*.AppImage /

+# syntax=docker/dockerfile:1
+# Windows x86_64 cross build from Linux (x86_64-pc-windows-gnu, mingw-w64):
+# a portable zip with the release zip's layout, for building and hand-testing
+# Windows binaries without a Windows box. NOT the shipped artifact - see
+# docker/README.md ("Windows").
+# Provenance: CamCraft's .github/workflows/release.yml (windows job's zip
+# layout), rustup's cross-compilation docs and the mingw-w64 toolchain.
+#
+#   docker build -f docker/windows-gnu.Dockerfile --output type=local,dest=dist .
+FROM ubuntu:22.04@sha256:076e7bf82319619f28dd0aa9c02ab34b055ad37100395b4f49a2ffba04fb5e11 AS toolchain
+
+ARG DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive
+# gcc-mingw-w64-x86-64 is the C cross compiler flecs_ecs_sys's cc build
+# needs (and the linker rustc's windows-gnu target calls); zip packs the
+# portable archive and unzip lists it back.
+RUN apt-get update \
+ && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
+        build-essential ca-certificates curl gcc-mingw-w64-x86-64 unzip zip \
+ && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*
+
+ARG RUST_TOOLCHAIN=1.99.1
+ENV RUSTUP_HOME=/usr/local/rustup \
+    CARGO_HOME=/usr/local/cargo \
+    PATH=/usr/local/cargo/bin:$PATH \
+    CARGO_TARGET_X86_64_PC_WINDOWS_GNU_LINKER=x86_64-w64-mingw32-gcc \
+    CC_x86_64_pc_windows_gnu=x86_64-w64-mingw32-gcc
+RUN curl --proto '=https' --tlsv1.2 -LfsS https://sh.rustup.rs \
+        | sh -s -- -y --no-modify-path --profile minimal \
+            --default-toolchain "$RUST_TOOLCHAIN" \
+            --target x86_64-pc-windows-gnu \
+ && rustc --version
+
+FROM toolchain AS build
+WORKDIR /src
+COPY . .
+ARG TARGET=x86_64-pc-windows-gnu
+RUN --mount=type=cache,target=/usr/local/cargo/registry \
+    --mount=type=cache,target=/src/target \
+    cargo build --locked --release --target "$TARGET" \
+        -p camcraft-ui -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-post \
+ && mkdir -p /out/bin \
+ && cp "target/$TARGET/release/camcraft-ui.exe" "target/$TARGET/release/camcraft-cli.exe" \
+       "target/$TARGET/release/post.exe" /out/bin/
+# The release.yml windows job's "Assemble portable zip" layout. The version
+# comes from the workspace manifest: a Linux host cannot run post.exe.
+RUN ver=$(sed -n 's/^version = "\([0-9.]*\)"$/\1/p' Cargo.toml | head -n1) \
+ && test -n "$ver" \
+ && stage="/dist/camcraft-$ver-win-x64-gnu" \
+ && mkdir -p "$stage/assets" \
+ && cp /out/bin/*.exe "$stage/" \
+ && for a in posts machines ui scripts themes; do cp -a "assets/$a" "$stage/assets/$a"; done \
+ && cp RELEASE_NOTES.md TESTING.md LICENSE "$stage/" \
+ && (cd /dist && zip -qr "camcraft-$ver-win-x64-gnu.zip" "camcraft-$ver-win-x64-gnu") \
+ && unzip -l "/dist/camcraft-$ver-win-x64-gnu.zip" | grep 'camcraft-ui.exe$'
+
+FROM scratch AS packages
+COPY --from=build /dist/*.zip /

+## #30 - Docker builds per shipped target
+
+**Decided:** a `docker/` directory with one Dockerfile per target that can
+honestly be built in a container - `linux.Dockerfile` (tar.gz, deb, rpm,
+AppImage, mirroring the release `linux` job) and `windows-gnu.Dockerfile`
+(an unofficial mingw cross-build portable zip) - plus `docker/build.sh` and
+a README table that names, for every shipped target, whether it builds in
+Docker and why not when it does not (snap, Flatpak, the msvc Windows zip +
+Inno installer, macOS). No workflow: the images are local tooling.
+
+**Why:** "Done means: documented or CI Docker build for each shipped target."
+The Linux packages are the only release assets a stock container can
+produce bit-for-bit from the release scripts. A local image costs no Actions
+minutes; a `docker.yml` would only re-run what release.yml's linux job
+already does on the same runner, so it was not added.
+
+**Pinning:** the base is `ubuntu:22.04` pinned by digest (the runner's
+distro: glibc 2.35, which the .deb's `libc6 (>= 2.35)` names). Rust is
+pinned by a build arg (default 1.99.1, current stable) because a container
+build should be reproducible, while the runner keeps its preinstalled
+stable; the two can drift by a release - accepted, and overridable.
+
+**Considered and dropped:**
+- cargo-xwin for an msvc cross build: it downloads Microsoft's CRT and
+  Windows SDK under their license into the image; not something to bake
+  into a distributable image, and Inno Setup / signtool would still need
+  Windows. The gnu zip is named `-win-x64-gnu` so it is never mistaken for
+  the release zip.
+- snap / Flatpak in Docker: need snapd / bwrap, i.e. a `--privileged`
+  container; left on the runner jobs, which only repackage the tarball.
+- macOS via osxcross: needs the Apple SDK, licensed for Apple hardware only.
+- A `workflow_dispatch` `docker.yml`: duplicates the release linux job and
+  spends minutes for nothing new.
+
+**Cost to change later:** adding a target is one more Dockerfile and a case
+in `docker/build.sh`. Bumping the base means a new digest; bumping Rust is
+the build arg default.
